criticalIssues.issue: CL-009 CRITICAL #1, UNRESOLVED AND NOT FIXABLE BY THE INTEGRATOR. 'Ours was Richard. Eleven years in. ... "With respect, some of us have been doing this a long time." It was the most expensive sentence anyone said that year.' is unchanged in final_article.md (verified by diff). A named, identifiable colleague in a team the piece states is fourteen people, with exact tenure, a verbatim quote, the labels 'the Diva' / 'the loudest cell' / 'the fever', and an implied financial-loss attribution. No consent is on file anywhere in this run. CL-009 is mandatory and sits at the top of the policy precedence order. I am not counsel and make no legal determination.
criticalIssues.repair: DO NOT ROUTE THIS TO THE INTEGRATOR. Route to the author and then to counsel. Author must either (a) produce written consent to the name, the quotation and the characterisation, or (b) remove the first name, the 'Eleven years in' tenure and the verbatim quote and recast him as an explicitly labelled composite. Changing the name alone does not fix it: the tenure plus the fourteen-person meeting identifies him to anyone who was in the room. Separately, 'the most expensive sentence anyone said that year' must be substantiated or softened, but only as part of the whole passage, not as a standalone word change. The integrator's decision to leave the passage untouched was correct: de-identifying on the author's behalf would have rewritten a piece that presents itself as a true first-hand account.

criticalIssues.issue: CL-009 CRITICAL #2, UNRESOLVED AND NOT FIXABLE BY THE INTEGRATOR. 'She started rehearsing meetings in the shower. She stopped asking questions, then stopped sleeping properly, then started wondering whether the problem was her.' and 'She told me later she'd drafted the resignation email twice.' are unchanged (verified by diff). criticalIssues.repair: Route to the author. Obtain her written, informed consent to this specific text, covering both the wellbeing details and the exclusion allegations; or remove the health details and exclusion specifics; or recast as an openly labelled composite. If the passage is reworked, also move the 'She told me later' attribution up, as Editorial recommended (one phrase, no rewrite).

criticalIssues.issue: CL-009 HIGH, UNRESOLVED. 'Names and some details have been changed.' remains the last line of the article. Compliance judged it insufficient in substance (it does not de-identify), misplaced (it arrives after the reader has taken the whole piece as literal, including the Richard passage), and ambiguous (a reader cannot tell which details changed, or whether 'Richard' is real).
criticalIssues.repair: Author only. She must state which is true — real account with changed names, or composite — then a precise note goes at or before first use. The integrator was right to refuse: Compliance itself says 'the author must confirm which statement is true', and writing either version would have invented a fact about the article's provenance.

criticalIssues.issue: AUTHENTICITY / FACTUAL INTEGRITY, UNRESOLVED. I independently confirmed that 'some of us have been doing this a long time' appears verbatim in the companion run 20261106-152245 ('The Most Dangerous Person in the Room', final_article.md line 40), spoken there by Graham at a different company. That run's SEO report also records the Diva/fever paragraph, the Great Corporate Unmasking paragraph and the Gallup sentence as word-for-word shared, and the two accounts give incompatible details (two months in, six-year process, four sign-offs, eleven days here; a 2019 wiki page, three departments, four days, an analyst named Dev there). This essay's entire authority rests on being first-hand. If both publish as true, a reader who sees both concludes one is invented.
criticalIssues.repair: Author decision affecting both runs: reconcile the accounts, or state once in each that they are composites, or move the shared quote and paragraphs out of one piece. Also settle sequencing and any first-publication/exclusivity terms with the target outlet before the companion goes live. The integrator flagged this correctly and was right not to silently edit either instance.

criticalIssues.issue: ADDED SENTENCE NEEDS AUTHOR SIGN-OFF (not drift, not a hallucination). 'Bullying is the extreme case of the same reflex.' is a sentence the author did not write. I traced it: it is verbatim from editorial.json's own recommendation ('Make the link honest with a half-sentence such as "Bullying is the extreme case of the same reflex."'). It asserts no checkable fact; it marks the WBI bullying figures as measuring an extreme of the essay's subject rather than the subject itself, which makes the paragraph more honest, not less. The author had already juxtaposed her story with the 32% figure, so the sentence names what she implied. Judgement: a necessary bridge, properly sourced to a specialist, correctly disclosed in the integration report, and legitimate editorial work — not the integrator arguing. It is still one interpretive sentence under a first-person byline.
criticalIssues.repair: Author approves the sentence as written or it comes out. No integrator action needed. If it comes out, the WBI figures need a different honest bridge, because without one the 32% and 62% read as measuring the expulsion of curious people, which they do not.

criticalIssues.issue: MEANING NARROWING THE AUTHOR MUST CONFIRM. The author's 'Gallup's 2026 workplace report puts it plainly: the technology works, but the bottom-line gains aren't arriving at scale' became '...shows the gap. In US organizations using AI, 65% of workers report a personal productivity gain. Only 12% strongly agree it has changed how work gets done.' Both figures are in fact_check.json's retrieved evidence and the rewrite is almost verbatim the Fact Checker's recommended action. The replacement is a different and narrower proposition than the author's (US-only; measures whether work changed, not bottom-line gains). I did NOT classify this as meaning drift, because the original put a sentence in a named third party's mouth that the Fact Checker could not find in the source, and CL-010 plus the honesty rules require removing a misattribution. A human may disagree with that call; the reasoning is on the record here.
criticalIssues.repair: Author confirms she is content with the narrower, sourced claim, or writes her own version of the bottom-line point with her own retrieved source. Her surrounding argument ('they bought the tools and pointed them at processes nobody had questioned') is untouched and carries the paragraph either way.

verdictRationale: REJECT, and the reason is consent, not craft. Publication is blocked by two unresolved CRITICAL CL-009 findings about identifiable real people, plus a HIGH disclosure finding, that only the author and counsel can clear. I deliberately did not use REPAIR: the integrator gets at most two attempts and there is nothing here it can usefully fix. It has already identified, documented and correctly refused to paper over every blocker. Sending this back for re-integration would burn attempts and risk pressuring an agent into de-identifying a real colleague on the author's behalf, which is exactly what Compliance says must not happen without her. Route to author, then counsel, then a brand director for CL-003, then back to QA. Do not re-run integration on this draft. The integration work itself is good and should be preserved intact.

dimensionEvidence.brandAdherence: 58. Earned: every deterministic voice rule is now green and I reproduced it independently (6/6, exit 0). The single VC-001 banned term 'at scale' is gone, and it went by replacing a misattributed paraphrase rather than by swapping a word. All three real VC-003 long sentences are split, with the opening's anaphora preserved intact. The docs/02-voice.md jargon row is applied correctly. CL-010 went from six unsourced figure clusters to five paragraphs all sourced or hedged. Brand Guardian scored the submission 66 with 8 mandatory violations; integration cleared the VC-001, all the VC-003s and the whole CL-010 set. Held down hard: five mandatory checklist rules remain unsatisfied — CL-009 at CRITICAL twice plus HIGH once, CL-008 (no limit stated), CL-003 (the one-line-paragraph column, unresolved disagreement), CL-027 (photo provenance incomplete while flagged cleared), and CL-047 open pending a narration decision. CL-009 is the most load-bearing rule in the checklist and it is the one that is broken. A piece that cannot satisfy the consent rule does not get a passing brand score however clean its sentences are.
dimensionEvidence.factualIntegrity: 76. Earned: the CONTRADICTED claim is gone with no number invented to replace it, which is the single most important thing that had to happen in this run. Zero fabricated sources — all four URLs trace to fact_check.json's retrieved evidence. Zero hallucinated statistics; I checked every figure in the final article against the evidence register one by one. The unverifiable 14%-witnessed clause was removed rather than published, and logged as restorable. 'The lowest since 2020' was corrected to 'matching the lowest level since 2020' because Gallup's trend table shows 20% in both years. The 23% figure recovered its comparison group. The 62% figure now says 'counting those who resign', which is what WBI actually measured. MIT Sloan is dated and attributed, with the Fact Checker's explicit warning against 'more likely to quit' respected. 'Global' was added to the manager figure. The Fact Checker scored the submission 40; this is a large, real improvement. Held down: (a) the companion-piece problem — a verbatim quote and three shared paragraphs across two pieces with incompatible details, one presented as true, unresolved and fatal to the first-hand framing if both ship; (b) three citations point at a Gallup slug the Fact Checker explicitly asked a human to confirm as canonical before linking, and the $10 trillion reference year is still open; (c) 'The person who gets attacked is usually the one who leaves' was kept at 'usually' against the Fact Checker's soften-to-often recommendation — the integrator's rationale (the 62% sits right beside it) is arguable, but 62% of targets losing a job, resignations included, is not the same proposition as the attacked person being the one who goes; (d) the whole anecdote rests on the author's word, acceptable with disclosure, except the disclosure is itself a HIGH finding.
dimensionEvidence.editorialQuality: 86. Editorial scored the submission 88 and the integration did it no harm, which is the hard part. The edits are surgical: 13 changes, not 30. The 29-word opening was split at its two 'whose' joints with not one word cut and the anaphora intact, so the fragments read as deliberate. The 49-word payoff was split into four sentences that keep the beat, with 'In our case' doing double duty as a CL-008 scope. 'Flip it around.' standing alone is better than 'Flip it around:'. The internal link solves the reader problem that Editorial's proposed cut was meant to solve, without cutting the author's callback. Nothing was flattened: the bank simile, the Diva disclaimer, 'hot, loud and absolutely convinced it's helping', both closes and all six takeaways survive, and the integrator refused to cut two takeaways on a stylistic preference two other specialists contradicted. Held down: the one added sentence, however well sourced to Editorial's own recommendation, is a beat the author did not write, in the most delicate paragraph in the piece; 'In our case,' is a small hedge-flatness in the story's payoff; the fever/cell metaphor slip is still there, deliberately; and the Gallup replacement is serviceable but flatter than the paraphrase it replaces — three figure-carrying sentences where there was one rhetorical one.
dimensionEvidence.seoGeoReadiness: 72. The channel is a publication pitch, and the integrator scoped to it correctly rather than decorating the piece: it took the one internal link the article already earned and declined the FAQ, the Article schema, the heading rewrites and the seoTitle/metaDescription/slug work that the SEO agent itself marked site-version-only, including its explicit advice against an FAQ on a guest column ('reads as SEO furniture'). dimensionEvidence.audienceUsefulness: 66. The audience is 'business leaders and the curious people they manage'. For the leader the piece is strong and now better evidenced: five sourced figures, a cost section that holds up, and six takeaways of which 2, 3, 5 and 6 are things a reader can act on, with takeaway 6 now carrying the manager-engagement source that is the premise for its advice. The integrator was right to reject glossing 'moat', 'compute' and 'commoditized' for this reader and right to keep 'like sediment, or emails from your bank'. Held down by two gaps it correctly identified and correctly refused to fill, because filling them is authorship: the reader who recognises themselves as the Diva gets a diagnosis and no route back, and the excluded reader whose manager is part of the problem gets recognition and no step they can take alone. The subtitle also promises a fatality the body never shows, which is a usefulness problem as much as a tone one — a reader who came for 'fatal' gets attrition multipliers. Two CRITICAL CL-009 findings about identifiable real people are unresolved and need the author and probably counsel. A HIGH disclosure finding needs a fact only the author knows. CL-027 photo provenance is marked cleared on an incomplete record and is owned outside this run. The 18 is not zero because the article is in a genuinely releasable state the moment consent exists: gates green, figures sourced, no fabricated citation, metadata complete, slug free of collisions, and a complete, named, owner-assigned list of what has to happen next. That list is the most valuable thing in the integration report.

whatTheIntegratorGotRight: Removed the CONTRADICTED statistic and substituted nothing. The tempting move was a sourced-looking number; it declined, on grounds I independently agree with.
